components.name: Primary Action Button
components.description: High-contrast action button used for primary GitHub Template invocation.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #ffffff; color: #070a11; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 11px 20px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #ffffff; cursor: pointer; transition: all 250ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #e2e8f0; transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Status Badge Danger

narrative.overview: Watchtower's design language evokes calm, high-precision telemetry and developer-first sovereignty. Inspired by modern developer observability tools and command consoles, the interface prioritizes information density, crisp typography, and verifiable truth over decorative fluff or neon tropes.
keyCharacteristics: Calm, High-Contrast Palette: Charcoal and navy obsidian ground accented by electric cyan, indigo, and status-verified hues.
Precision Typography: European grotesque display (Schibsted Grotesk) paired with purpose-built monospace (JetBrains Mono) strictly for code, versions, and metrics.
Authentic Demonstrations: Realistic console previews displaying verifiable OSV advisories and semver diffs.
Zero Noise / Zero Slop: No fake AI claims, no exaggerated glowing gradients, and no unsolicited decoration.

rules.name: The Monospace Discipline Rule
rules.body: Monospace typography is reserved strictly for code, package identifiers, semver numbers, and terminal telemetry.

rules.name: The Fact-First Rule
rules.body: Color badges communicate verified status categories with text labels alongside color, never relying on color alone.

dos: Do preserve the strict read-only, developer-first voice.
Do ensure all tabular data uses tabular numerals and monospace version tags.
Do maintain high text contrast ratios (minimum 4.5:1 for body copy).
Do include both GitHub Template and VS Code Extension actions prominently.
donts: Don't mention AI analysis, automatic pull requests, automatic upgrades, or drift/health scores.
Don't use neon glowing borders, fake hacker command lines, or gratuitous particle animations.
Don't hide or obscure the zero hosting cost / data ownership guarantee.
